chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ismail and Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Sufyan ibn al-Simṭ, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'When you enter from the second door on the right side of the Masjid, count five pillars, two of them in the shade and three in the courtyard, and at the third is the prayer place of Ibrahim (peace be upon him), and it is the fifth from the wall.'

He (the narrator) said: 'So when it was the days of Abu al-Abbas, Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) entered from the Door of Al-Feel, and he moved left when he entered from the door, and he prayed by the fourth pillar, and it was parallel to the fifth. So I said, 'Is that not the pillar of Ibrahim (peace be upon him)?' So he said to me, 'Yes.'

key_terms.مَيْمَنَةِ الْمَسْجِدِ: the right side of the Masjid

ai.seo_question: Where is the prayer place of Ibrahim (AS) located in the Grand Masjid of Kufa?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi precisely locates the prayer spot of Prophet Ibrahim (peace be upon him) within the Grand Mosque of Kufa, detailing the architectural markers of the pillars and their relation to the courtyard's shade. It further records Imam al-Sadiq’s (peace be upon him) confirmation of this location during the Abbasid era, highlighting the continuity of sacred geography and the scholarly tradition of preserving specific sites of merit (fadl) for devotional practice.
